newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends firm on seedings data, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends firm on seedings data, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a slower-than-expected seeding progress last week for the U.S. crop, traders said.

USDA Monday said as of Sunday, 18 percent of the U.S. crop had been planted, below trade expectations for 20 to 25 percent. The 18 percent seeding tally was below the 21 percent pace of a year ago but above the five-year average of 15 percent.
However, some traders were skeptical of the seedings figure and said current warmer and drier weather was allowing aggressive seeding of the U.S. crop.
"Eighteen percent is lower than they were looking for and probably more than that was planted," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

But ideas that corn seedings would soon slow in the Midwest circulated. Two storm systems were forecast to spread through the Midwest beginning late Tuesday which should curb planting in much of Iowa, northern Illinois and northern Indiana this week, forecasters said.
Corn closed 1/4 to 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with May up 3/4 at $2.91-1/2. New crop December was up 1/4 at $2.74-3/4.

The corn market also was underpinned by slow farmer selling and the prospects of light to zero deliveries to be posted against the May contract. Wednesday is first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT May contracts.

In spread trading, Griffin Trading spread 10.0 million bushels of July/May at even money, Continental Grain did 10.0 million May/July at even money to 1/2 cent premium July, traders said. Farmers Commodities Corp did two million bushels of July/May at 1/4 cent, premium May, traders said.
In outright trading, FIMAT Futures bought 12.0 million bushels of December, Griffin Trading bought four million bushels of December and Refco Inc bought four million bushels of July, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold 3.5 million bushels of December, Dean Witter and R.J. O'Brien each sold two million July and Tenco Inc sold two million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 87,000 contracts, below the 103,800 traded Monday.

In corn options, ABN-Amro, The Chicago Corp sold 1,500 December $3.20 calls at 7-1/2 to 7-3/4 cents, Lind Waldock bought 600 July $3.40 calls at 1-1/4 cents and Rand Financial bought 500 December $2.60 puts at 10-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, below the 18,682 traded Monday.
